Day 1
From Hotel: 10 min → di Rosa Center for Contemporary Art
1. di Rosa Center for Contemporary Art
Opened to the public in 1997 by collector Rene di Rosa, this 217-acre estate holds approximately 1,600 works of art by Northern California artists. The property includes multiple galleries, a sculpture meadow, and Winery Lake.

Sparkling wine estate founded in 1987 as a joint venture between Champagne Taittinger and Kobrand Corporation. The château-style building sits on a 138-acre hillside estate in the Los Carneros AVA with panoramic views toward San Francisco Bay.

3. Stag's Leap Wine Cellars
Founded in 1970 by Warren Winiarski, this winery gained international recognition when its 1973 Cabernet Sauvignon took first place among red wines at the 1976 Judgment of Paris blind tasting. The S.L.V. estate vineyard sits on gravel benchlands above the valley floor in the Stags Leap District.

Day 2
From Hotel: 24 min → Beringer Vineyards
1. Beringer Vineyards
Established in 1876, Beringer is the oldest continuously operating winery in Napa Valley. The estate centers on the Rhine House, a 17-room mansion built in 1883–1884. The property is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and holds California Historical Landmark status No. 814.

23 min → Castello di Amorosa
2. Castello di Amorosa
A 121,000-square-foot, 107-room castle modeled on 13th-century Tuscan and Lombard architecture, built by Dario Sattui between 1993 and 2007. The structure includes a Great Hall, drawbridge, moat, dungeon, and torture chamber. The castle houses winery production facilities and tasting rooms across four floors.

3. Robert Mondavi Winery
Founded in 1966 by Robert Mondavi, this winery is credited with establishing Napa Valley as a world-class wine region. The estate encompasses the historic To Kalon vineyard, originally planted in 1868, and pioneered varietal wine labeling in California.

4. Opus One Winery
Founded in 1979 as a partnership between Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild. The winery produces a single Grand Vin Bordeaux-style blend. The semicircular building, designed by architect Scott Johnson, was completed in 1991 on 170 acres in Oakville.

From Hotel: 38 min → Chateau Montelena
1. Chateau Montelena
Founded in 1882, Chateau Montelena's 1973 Chardonnay won first place among white wines at the 1976 Judgment of Paris. The estate surrounds Jade Lake, a Chinese garden with a pagoda added in 1958, set against the stone château at the north end of Napa Valley.

8 min → Schramsberg Vineyards
2. Schramsberg Vineyards
Founded in 1862, Schramsberg became California's first premium sparkling wine estate when Jack and Jamie Davies revived it in 1965. The hillside caves, dug in the 1870s, are on the National Register of Historic Places. Schramsberg sparkling wines were served at Nixon's 1972 state dinner in Beijing.

10 min → Sterling Vineyards
3. Sterling Vineyards
Established in 1964 on a 300-foot knoll above Calistoga, Sterling Vineyards is reached via a gondola from the valley floor. The white Mediterranean-style buildings were completed in 1973. The self-guided tour includes barrel rooms, vineyards, and views across the northern valley from multiple terraces.

Local Tastes
Napa Cabernet Sauvignon
Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon is the region's benchmark varietal — full-bodied with concentrated dark fruit and structured tannins. The To Kalon vineyard in Oakville is the most recognized Cab source in California.
Robert Mondavi Winery · Oakville
Farm-to-Table Cuisine
Napa Valley's restaurant culture is built around direct relationships between chefs and local farms, vineyards, and ranches. Seasonal menus change based on what's available from within the valley.
Oxbow Public Market · Downtown Napa
Wild Mustard Flowers
Each winter, wild mustard flowers bloom between vineyard rows, covering the valley in yellow from January through March. The Napa Valley Mustard Festival runs February–March with wine, food, and art events.
Napa Valley vineyard rows · Yountville area

Day Trips by Train
Martinez Station → San Francisco · 1 hr 15 min
Capitol Corridor train to Emeryville, then the Amtrak bus shuttle to downtown San Francisco. The Ferry Building, Embarcadero, and Union Square are all within walking distance of the shuttle terminus.
book at: Amtrak or Omio
Martinez Station → Sacramento · 1 hr 15 min
Capitol Corridor or San Joaquins east to Sacramento. Old Sacramento waterfront and the California State Capitol are accessible on foot at the station.
book at: Amtrak or Omio

Worth Knowing

Napa Valley is 30 miles long and rarely more than 5 miles wide. What it produces per acre — in wine, restaurants, and culinary intent — has no real equivalent in the United States.

The valley earned that reputation by being meticulous: every winery you visit here made deliberate decisions about soil, rootstock, clone, and canopy management that most wine regions wouldn't bother with. Robert Mondavi understood in 1966 that quality wine needed to be taken seriously in California the way it was in Burgundy — not imitated, but held to the same standard. That conviction is still visible in what you drink here.

The French Laundry's two-month-out reservation system is not a stunt. It reflects the same seriousness applied to food: the menus change daily, the produce comes from the restaurant's own garden, and the kitchen works at a level that makes most fine dining look approximate. The fact that it exists three blocks from your hotel — that Yountville, a town of 3,000 people, contains one of the most considered restaurants on earth — tells you something about what this valley decided to become.
